newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says helicopter crashed on Iraq operation.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says helicopter crashed on Iraq operation.

text.p: Turkey's military headquarters said on Sunday an army helicopter had crashed, killing the two pilots, during the armed forces' incursion into northern Iraq in pursuit of Kurdish rebels.
"A helicopter belonging to the army crashed because of a technical fault on May 18 at 7:30 a.m. (0430 GMT) south of the Cukurca area of Hakkari province," a statement from the general staff said.
The five-day-old Turkish operation against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas in the region has drawn criticism from Ankara's Western allies and the United Nations.
Turkish troops have been fighting PKK rebels mainly in the Sinaht border area since they poured into the area early on Wednesday.
The military has said they have killed 902 guerrillas so far for the loss of 12 members of the security forces.

F-16 jets bombed rebel positions in the northern Iraqi mountains, while a column of Turkish tanks moved northeast along the road from the town of Dohuk to Amadiya in what appeared to be preparations for a second prong of attack.
